episode_title: April Dunford on Obviously Awesome Positioning, Category Creation, and Differentiation
guest_bio: World-renowned positioning expert and author of Obviously Awesome.
text: Positioning is not what you do to your product; it is the mental context you set in your customer's mind. The fundamental starting point of positioning is understanding competitive alternatives: 'What would the customer use if your product didn't exist?' In most enterprise software, the true competitor is not another startup—it's Excel sheets, manual intern labor, or doing nothing. If you position against the wrong alternative, your unique features won't make sense to buyers.

episode_title: April Dunford on Obviously Awesome Positioning, Category Creation, and Differentiation
guest_bio: World-renowned positioning expert and author of Obviously Awesome.
text: Don't create a category unless you have $50M in venture funding and 5 years to educate the market. Creating a new category requires teaching people a new problem exists, which is brutally slow and expensive. It is 10x faster and cheaper to position as a sub-segment or specialized solution in an existing, well-understood market (e.g. 'CRM for Venture Capitalists' rather than 'Relationship Intelligence Ecosystem').
